summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY (about 10% volume, 7% price) while EBITDA margin fell to about 14.4% on raw material spike.
summary.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY in Q1 FY27, with roughly 10% from volumes and about 7% from price increases taken in April and mid-May. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.4%, which management attributed to 6-7 percentage points of raw material cost inflation (VAM spike linked to West Asia tensions) plus about 3-4 points of aggressive dealer-meet and sales promotion spend. Management guided back to a 22-25% EBITDA range longer term and said it is too early to commit to 28-29% in Q2. Working capital weakened, with receivables around INR 145-150 crore (debtor days above 150) and inventory higher, and management targets 120 days over the next two to three quarters.

financial_highlights.change: hit by 6-7 pts raw material cost and 3-4 pts promotion spend

financial_highlights.value: about INR 360 crore annualised (cited by analyst; ~INR 90 crore per quarter)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 INR 314 crore, FY25 INR 285 crore, FY24 INR 258-260 crore
debtor days above 150 vs target of 120

segments.name: Wood adhesives (Euro brand)
segments.commentary: Core business; management cites brand strength, distribution reach and carpenter trust. Registered carpenters rose to 210,000, about 10,000 added in the quarter.

segments.name: OEM / modular kitchens and furniture
segments.commentary: About 6% of revenue currently; management targets 10-12% over time, with team build-out in Bangalore, Telangana and Delhi.

guidance_outlook: Brownfield expansion from 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes per month expected operational within one to two months; management says it can support INR 600-650 crore revenue from the existing plant.
Longer-term target of INR 500 crore revenue by end FY29 at 23-25% EBITDA margin, requiring 15-20% volume growth; management also refers to a INR 1,000 crore vision.
EBITDA margin guided at 22-25% longer term; management said it is too early to say whether Q2 can reach 28-29%.
Sales promotion expense for FY27 expected at about 10% above last year's INR 45-50 crore, scaling with volume.
Advertising and branding targeted at 6-7% of revenue for the year (currently about 4%).
Employee cost expected to settle at 11-13% of revenue per management.
Greenfield plant: initial capex INR 45-50 crore, funded from internal accruals, to add 1,500 tpm in phases; timing not specified.
Debtor days target of about 120 within two to three quarters.
NSE listing said to be in process and expected within the quarter; buyback discussed internally but no decision.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion from 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes per month; management said about 80% of work is done and capacity is ready within one to two months.
Q1 utilisation about 65-70% (earlier stated as about 60%); average monthly volume about 1,300 tonnes, March peak about 2,400 tonnes.
Brownfield capex about INR 7 crore, described as asset-light.
Greenfield: INR 45-50 crore initial capex (about 50% land, 50% construction, balance machinery), adds 1,500 tpm in phases.
Raw material inventory was about 30 days; management has contracted 90-day supply for Q2.
demand_pricing: VAM (key raw material) averaged about INR 75-78/kg, spiked to INR 170-180/kg in late March, eased to INR 135-150, and is now about INR 100/kg.
Price hikes: about 4% in April and about 11% in mid-May; management says about 7% realised for Q1 and no further hike in Q2.
Volume response: customers delayed projects in late May; demand recovered from June and July described as good; volume growth of about 10% maintained.
Retailer margin passed on is 7-13% (about 11-12% average); about 13,000 retailers served directly via 54 branches across about 15 states.
Competition: management said market leaders also raised prices and maintained EBITDA, which it read as rational pricing.
Bad debt historically below 0.5% per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue plan before Greenfield expansion, and what margins are expected by FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the brownfield 3,500 tpm can generate INR 600-650 crore revenue and the Greenfield is a longer-term step; EBITDA guidance remains 22-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sales promotion and employee costs rise sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales force raised from 520 to 562, new hires and April appraisals; about INR 4.5 crore spent on 54 dealer meets in 45 days (vs about INR 2 crore for 30 meets last year).

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 margins rebound to 28-29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; management is targeting the 22-25% range longer term and said raw material cooling has begun but not returned to earlier levels.

qa_highlights.question: What share of growth came from volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% from volume and about 7% from price in Q1; management expects price contribution may not persist if realisations normalise, and aims for 15-20% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth weak in FY24-FY26 after the COVID-era surge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a consolidation phase after an 80% jump to INR 181 crore; it cited FY25 and FY26 growth of about 9-10% and two quarters above 15% in the last four.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and debtor days outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables about INR 145-150 crore; target 120 days in two to three quarters, with slower push to protect retailer relationships in newer states; cited bad debt below 0.5%.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from VAM volatility; the 90-day supply contracts were only signed for Q2, and the EBITDA recovery depends on them.
Receivable days above 150 versus 120 target, concentrated in newer states; working capital and inventory build-up.
Demand elasticity after 7% price hike; management said some projects were held in late May and June.
Whether volumes ramp into the 3,500 tpm capacity; Q1 utilisation about 65-70%, with the 600-650 crore revenue claim not yet tested.
Sustained high employee and promotion spend without commensurate volume gains.
Possible price rollback if realisations normalise, which management said it may need to take.
NSE listing and buyback decision still pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but noticeably cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term margin (declined to commit to Q2 28-29%) and on receivables timing. Answers on revenue capacity conversion and the INR 500 crore target were loosely framed and required clarification from analysts.
key_quotes: Since we are light on inventory of raw materials as well as finished goods, we had to take the impact of the sharp rise in the raw materials price.
So, it is too early to say that we can rather maintain the 28% EBITDA into quarter 2. But as I said that about a longer term, we are confident about the 22% to 25% EBITDA margin.
So, that can generate almost INR 600 crores to INR 650 crores of revenue from here.
So, I think we require two to three quarters to maintain and to get down this debtor cycles.

growth.why: Management targets INR 500 crore revenue by end FY29 (about 15-20% volume growth) and says the brownfield expansion from 2,000 to 3,500 tpm, about 80% done, supports INR 600-650 crore revenue, with utilisation at 65-70%; the backing is capacity and demand but without firm order or contract numbers, so clarity is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margin fell to ~14.4% on 6-7 pts raw material and 3-4 pts promotion spend; VAM has eased from INR 170-180 to ~INR 100/kg and 90-day contracts are signed for Q2, but management says 22-25% is a longer-term range and Q2 28-29% is unconfirmed (brief says 23-25% Q2 in one quote, so guidance is conflicting).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Brownfield expansion from 2,000 to 3,500 tpm is about 80% done and management says it is ready within one to two months; Q1 utilisation is only 65-70% so the new capacity is not yet a constraint.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume grew ~10% in Q1 with demand described as good from June-July, and management aims for 15-20% volume growth to reach INR 500 crore by FY29; utilisation at 65-70% leaves headroom.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 65-70% against 2,000 tpm (average ~1,300 tonnes/month, March peak ~2,400) means no near-term capex need, but a greenfield plant of 1,500 tpm with INR 45-50 crore initial capex is already planned with no timing given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on near-term margin and said the price contribution (~7%) may not persist and a rollback is possible if realisations normalise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin is 14.4% vs 22-25% guided longer term, management declined to commit to 28-29% for Q2, and VAM is still ~INR 100/kg against INR 75-78 earlier; 90-day supply contracts cover only Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Product launches were not discussed; OEM/modular push is a segment build-out, not a new product.

rows.label: Debtor days back to 120 from above 150
rows.why: Receivables are INR 145-150 crore with debtor days above 150 vs a 120-day target, and management has set a 2-3 quarter timeline, though it will go slower to protect retailer relationships in newer states.

rows.label: OEM/modular kitchens share rise to 10-12%
rows.why: OEM is about 6% of revenue today with team build-out in Bangalore, Telangana and Delhi, but no timeline or order numbers were given.

rows.label: NSE listing and buyback
rows.why: NSE listing is said to be in process and expected within the quarter, while the buyback is only discussed internally with no decision, so the listing is more firm than the buyback.
